Realizing this potential requires electrocatalytic systems that achieve technoeconomic viability, which is linked to performance metrics such as activity, selectivity, and stability. Their deployment is constrained by two coupled challenges: incomplete mechanistic understanding of dynamic electrochemical interfaces and slow manual workflows that cannot efficiently explore the high-dimensional design spaces of catalysts, electrolytes, and operating parameters. In electrochemical reactions, performance across its many dimensions emerges from the evolving interplay of catalyst structure and local reaction environment at polarized interfaces. Advancing electrocatalytic performance therefore requires tools that can both reveal and enable control over the evolving catalyst-electrolyte interface during operation. He develops new technological applications based on insights into quantum mechanics and tries to understand the complexity of complex quantum systems. It is characteristic for his work to make use of tools of theoretical physics and mathematics, but to apply them to pragmatically motivated problems. He is one of the most visible and prolific researchers in his field. On the basis of his work, he has been awarded two ERC grants, a EURYI award (the predecessor of the ERC StG), and a Google NISQ award. events.title: La ciutat com a espai públic: una mirada des de la filosofia - Conferència cancel·lada
events.label: Educació
events.summary: La ciutat com a espai públic: una mirada des de la filosofia - Conferència cancel·lada. Educació
events.detail_text: El catedràtic de filosofia social i política Daniel Innerarity imparteix la conferència inaugural del nou curs acadèmic de l'Escola Tècnica Superior d'Arquitectura del Vallès (ETSAV-UPC). En aquesta ocasió, Innerarity reflexiona sobre la ciutat com a espai públic i les seves transformacions. Amb tota la seva ambivalència, la ciutat ha estat l'element integrador per antonomàsia de les societats, gràcies a la seva centralitat, densitat i contraposició respecte dels seus voltants rurals. Innerarity analitza com aquesta funció integradora es troba desafiada des de fa temps per diverses transformacions de la nostra manera de viure, principalment pels canvis en la seva configuració espacial i, ara, pel nou entorn digital en què vivim.

events.title: The next frontier in gravitational-wave physics
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: The next frontier in gravitational-wave physics
events.speakers: Jose Maria Ezquiaga, Niels Bohr Institute
events.detail_text: Abstract : Our Universe is still largely a mystery. Elusive dark matter shapes cosmic structures, while the Universe expands at a rate that we struggle to understand. Unraveling these fundamental open questions demands a deeper look into the distant cosmos, where gravitational waves from stellar-mass binary black holes offer a unique observational window. Unlike electromagnetic signals, gravitational waves traverse the Universe without alteration, except for gravitational lensing. Their long wavelengths make them subject to diffraction by cosmic structures, providing an unprecedented opportunity to map dark matter and test the foundations of gravity. If we can recover these lensed signals, we gain a cosmic magnifying glass to observe the most distant black hole mergers and illuminate their origins. Current gravitational-wave observations have already produced puzzling lensing candidates (e.g., GW231123), and the first definitive detections are expected very soon. In this talk, I will explain why gravitational-wave lensing is uniquely informative, outline how deep‑learning methods can accelerate its discovery, and show what the first detections could reveal about dark‑matter substructure and astrophysical black hole formation channels. This seminar is part of the “Holography in the Gravitational Wave Era” (HOLOGW) project, with Grant Agreement n. 1011419092, funded by the European Union / ERC.

events.title: ANTONIO ACÍN SUMMER LECTURE: Quantum Information Without Trust
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: ANTONIO ACÍN SUMMER LECTURE: Quantum Information Without Trust
events.detail_text: Skills Training > Lectures and Tutorials September 8, 2026 ANTONIO ACÍN SUMMER LECTURE: Quantum Information Without Trust Hour: From 12:00h to 13:00h Place: Yellow Lecture Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google SUMMER LECTURE: Quantum Information Without Trust ANTONIO ACÍN ICFO - Quantum Information Theory Quantum technologies promise new ways of communicating and processing information that are impossible using classical devices. But how can we trust quantum devices if they are so hard to simulate classically? Device-independent quantum information processing offers the answer: instead of trusting how a device is built, we can verify its behaviour purely from the statistics of its outputs. The talk introduces the basic ideas behind the device-independent framework, focusing on how “quantum correlations” — patterns of outcomes that cannot be explained by classical physics — can serve as a guarantee of correct and secure operation. Protocols for secure randomness generation and key distribution are presented. Finally, it is discussed how concepts and tools initially derived for device-independent quantum information applications open new perspectives for the understanding of quantum many-body systems. events.detail_text: Seminars September 8, 2026 STEFAN BÄUML SEMINAR: Updates on the Bound Key Conjecture Hour: From 11:00h to 12:00h Place: Blue Lecture Room Share Outlook iCalendar Google SEMINAR: Updates on the Bound Key Conjecture STEFAN BÄUML Freie Universität Berlin A long standing open problem in the theory of quantum resources is whether there exist states that need quantum key as a resource when being created using only local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but from which no quantum key is obtainable using only LOCC. Motivated by the analogous term in entanglement theory such states would be called bound key states. A related question is whether there exist entangled states from which no cryptographic key can be distilled, or conversely whether the distillable key is faithful as a measure of entanglement. We refer to such states mathematical bound key. In this work we shed some light on those questions, discussing the non-triviality of defining a measure of key cost in analogy to the entanglement cost. We provide show a surprising dichotomic relationship between the existence of mathematical bound key and an asymptotic version of the bound key conjecture. We also generalise the concept of bound key to the multipartite setting of conference key agreement and discuss ways in which a key cost can be defined. events.title: Critical collapse with relativistic elastic matter
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Critical collapse with relativistic elastic matter
events.speakers: Jorge Rocha, ISCTE-Instituto Universitário de Lisboa
events.detail_text: Abstract : After giving quick overviews of critical collapse and a formalism of relativistic elasticity, I will discuss recent work aimed at analyzing critical collapse with elastic materials. It is well-known that gravitational collapse in (non-elastic) perfect fluid models displays emergent continuous self-similarity at the threshold of black hole formation. Such matter models can be extended to include relativistic elasticity effects, and continuous self-similar configurations arise in this context when choosing a scale-invariant elastic matter model. A discrete family of such threshold solutions is determined numerically by solving an associated boundary value problem. I will present various results for these modes and discuss how their properties are affected by elasticity parameters, namely the shear index and the Poisson ratio.

events.title: Salut
events.label: Institut d’Humanitats
events.detail_text: Ens acostem al concepte de salut amb el filòsof Angel Puyol en el nou curs del cicle Lèxic quotidià de filosofia , dirigit per Daniel Gamper i que proposa interpretacions filosòfiques sobre temes de la vida. La paraula salut prové del llatí salus , que significa ‘salvació, benestar, prosperitat’, i no només absència de malaltia o funcionalitat de l’organisme, tal com es considera en el paradigma biomèdic. En canvi, l’OMS ofereix avui dia una definició més en sintonia amb l’origen romà de la paraula, i vincula la salut al benestar físic, psíquic i social de les persones; en realitat, a un benestar complet, sencer, d’acord ara amb l’arrel indoeuropea de la paraula, sol -. Estar sa és gaudir d’un benestar sòlid, intacte. Però això genera una certa tensió filosòfica en el concepte: com més reduïm la salut a la biomedicina, més lluny estem de viure una vida realment saludable, però com més l’associem al benestar, més confonem la salut amb la felicitat. A aquesta tensió se n’hi afegeix una altra de més contemporània: malgrat el que ens diuen la medicina i la societat individualista, la salut no és un assumpte individual. La salut de cadascú no pot anar bé si no va bé la de tothom, inclosos els altres animals i els ecosistemes. No hi ha salvació —ni vida saludable— fora de la comunitat. I encara hi ha un tercer atzucac relacionat amb la salut. events.title: Visita a «El culte a la bellesa» amb Irene Pujadas
events.label: Visites El culte a la bellesa
events.summary: Visita a «El culte a la bellesa» amb Irene Pujadas. Visites El culte a la bellesa
events.speakers: Irene Pujadas Produeix Amb el suport de Aquesta activitat forma part de: El culte a la bellesa Mirades laterals
events.detail_text: L’escriptora Irene Pujadas proposa una visita a l’exposició que explora les formes d’amagar-se, camuflar-se o desaparèixer davant les pressions i expectatives que sovint condicionen la manera com ens mostrem als altres. Disfresses, transformisme, desaparicions. En un món arrebossat d'expectatives i pressions constants sobre l’aparença, quin potencial pot tenir l’acte d’amagar-se? Quines formes pot prendre la tècnica del camuflatge? És un estat necessàriament passiu o d’aquest amagatall se'n pot derivar una nova forma d’estar al món? Fins i tot una idea de bellesa més lliure i menys constreta? Farem un recorregut per l’exposició centrant-nos en la idea de l’amagatall, d'artistes que han buscat maneres de «no ser vistes» i de protegir-se de la mirada dels altres. Repassarem algunes obres de l’exposició que toquen aquesta idea i la salpebrarem amb obres terceres, tant d'art com de literatura. Amb Mirades laterals , el CCCB aposta per expandir el relat expositiu a través de veus que, amb la seva singularitat, ens ajuden a mirar, i a mirar-nos, des d’altres llocs, i que converteixen l’exposició en un espai viu, interrogatiu i obert a múltiples formes de sentit.

Although this property makes electron beams uniquely suited to address confined optical modes, their full potential for technological applications is still being actively developed. This Thesis aims to contribute to this effort by exploring novel phenomena that arise when electron beams are incorporated into different optical systems. Chapter 2 explores electron-driven excitation of surface polaritons through resonant scatterers placed near polariton-supporting materials. events.title: Primordial Black Holes and Early-Universe Cosmology
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Primordial Black Holes and Early-Universe Cosmology
events.speakers: Albert Escrivà, Asia Pacific Center for Theoretical Physics
events.detail_text: Abstract : In this talk, I will give an overview of primordial black holes, from their origins to their present role in early-Universe cosmology. I will focus in particular on my research on PBH formation, highlighting some of the main results and developments achieved so far. I will then discuss open problems and future research directions, including connections with gravitational-wave cosmology. Finally, I will discuss how these research directions could fit within and contribute to the research activities in cosmology and gravitation at the ICC/UB.

events.title: Quantum and Holographic Aspects of Black Holes
events.label: Thesis Defence
events.summary: Thesis Defence: Quantum and Holographic Aspects of Black Holes
events.detail_text: Abstract : This thesis explores the quantum nature of black holes using the gravitational path integral and the holographic AdS/CFT framework. It focuses on three main questions: how quantum effects modify black hole geometries, how black hole entropy arises from microscopic quantum states, and how near-extremal rotating black holes behave at low temperature. First, it shows that quantum backreaction can create new black hole solutions, including charged black holes that are impossible in classical gravity. Second, it studies semiclassical black hole states and finds that Euclidean wormholes create correlations between them. Taking these overlaps into account gives a number of states consistent with the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, suggesting that gravitational path integrals can encode black hole microstates. Finally, the thesis studies rotating black holes near extremality and shows that their low-temperature behavior can be described by a two-dimensional theory related to the Schwarzian action. events.title: Rare decays with missing energy and new invisible scalars
events.label: Seminar
events.summary: Seminar: Rare decays with missing energy and new invisible scalars
events.detail_text: Abstract : We discuss possible light invisible scalars in the context of rare decays with missing energy. We first explore the windows remaining in B to K + inv and K to pi + inv decay modes. We construct simple UV-complete extensions and discuss some resulting phenomenology in parameter regions where the scalars are consistent with dark matter constraints. For these and heavier scalars, we study the consequences of these models in monojet events.

events.title: Visita guiada a l’«Exposició de varietats antifeixistes»
events.label: Amics CCCB
events.summary: Visita guiada a l’«Exposició de varietats antifeixistes». Amics CCCB
events.detail_text: Maria Canelles, directora d’Arts Visuals de la Fundació Joan Brossa, ens guiarà per l’univers compartit de Pere Portabella i Joan Brossa en una visita exclusiva a una exposició que explora les relacions entre art, dissidència i compromís polític. L'«Exposició de varietats antifeixistes» és una mostra produïda pel Centre de les Arts Lliures de la Fundació Joan Brossa amb motiu del centenari de Pere Portabella. Comissariada per Marcelo Expósito, l'exposició reuneix documents, obres i materials procedents dels arxius de Pere Portabella i Joan Brossa, així com contribucions d'altres procedències. El projecte ofereix una mirada coral sobre l'antifeixisme, l'experimentació artística i el paper de la cultura com a espai de transformació política. Al llarg del recorregut aprofundirem en el diàleg entre els dos creadors i en les connexions entre arxius, memòries i pràctiques artístiques que han contribuït a imaginar formes de resistència i canvi social.
